subject: Mathematics
exam_context: JEE Main 2026 (Paper 1, B.E./B.Tech) — Mathematics section only, 25 questions/100 marks
data_provenance: Estimated from PYQ-trend analysis and chapter-wise-weightage/marks trackers aggregated across the 2025 and 2026 (Jan + Apr) sessions (not official NTA data), cross-referenced against multiple careers360 community weightage tables and marks breakdowns; last grounded Sep 2026. Some careers360 marks tables report Limit/Continuity/Differentiability, Integral Calculus and Differential Equations as a combined 'differential and integral calculus' figure — this file disaggregates that estimate across X07/X08/X09 using proportions seen in other trackers. Individual-session weightage varies shift to shift; treat these as multi-session averages for question-bank planning, not a guarantee of any single paper's composition.

X01.notes: Foundational unit, often fused into a function/relation classification question; ~4-5% weightage.

X02.notes: Nature-of-roots and modulus/argument numericals are the dominant archetype; ~8-10% weightage combining both halves of this unit.

X03.notes: One of the highest-weightage Maths chapters at ~13-14% per multiple trackers; adjoint/inverse and consistency-of-equations numericals recur every session.

X04.notes: Lower-weightage standalone unit (~3%) but frequently fused into Probability or Binomial Theorem questions.

X05.chapter: Binomial Theorem and its Simple Applications
X05.notes: Low standalone weightage (~3%); general-term and middle-term numericals are the standard archetype.

X06.notes: Low standalone weightage (~3%) after the 2025 removal of special-series-sum content; AP/GM-mean numericals dominate.

X07.notes: Maxima/minima and tangent-normal application questions recur heavily; ~11-12% weightage.

X08.notes: The single highest-weightage Maths chapter at ~13-14%; definite-integral evaluation and area-under-curve numericals dominate.

X09.notes: Separation-of-variables and linear first-order DE numericals are the standard archetype; ~5-6% weightage.

X10.notes: Consistently the single highest-weightage Maths unit across trackers at ~18%; straight-line, circle and conic-section (parabola/ellipse/hyperbola) numericals dominate.

X11.notes: Reduced scope after the 2025 rationalisation removed line-plane intersection content; direction-cosines and shortest-distance-between-skew-lines numericals remain the standard archetype. Often reported jointly with X12 as 'Vector & 3D' (~11% combined).

X12.notes: Scalar/vector product numericals are the standard archetype. Often reported jointly with X11 as 'Vector & 3D' (~11% combined).

X13.notes: Conditional-probability (Baye's theorem) and standard-deviation-of-grouped-data numericals dominate; ~7-9% weightage.

X14.notes: Trigonometric-equation-solving and inverse-trig-function-property questions dominate after the 2025 removal of heights-and-distances; ~10% weightage.

broad_category_weightage_pct.note: Coarser cross-check figures, approximate % share of the 25-question Maths section, synthesised from multiple 2025-2026 PYQ trend/marks sources. Rounds do not sum to exactly 100% because chapter-boundary reporting (e.g. whether Vector and 3D Geometry are combined) is inconsistent across sources.

marking_scheme.source_note: Confirmed via multiple Sep 2026 sources reporting on the actual Jan 2026 and Apr 2026 JEE Main sessions.
marking_scheme.section_a_mcq: 20 single-correct MCQs per subject; +4 for a correct answer, -1 for an incorrect answer, 0 if unattempted.
marking_scheme.section_b_numerical: 5 numerical-value questions per subject, all compulsory (the earlier 'attempt any 5 of 10' choice was removed starting with the 2025 pattern); +4 for a correct answer, -1 for an incorrect answer, 0 if unattempted. This differs from pre-2025 sessions, when numerical questions carried no negative marking.
marking_scheme.question_types_used: Single-correct MCQ and numerical-value only. JEE Main does NOT use multiple-correct MCQs or matrix-match questions — those formats are exclusive to JEE Advanced.
